solutions.blurb: The Ocean Cleanup removes legacy plastic from ocean garbage patches and intercepts it in rivers: more than 65 million kilograms caught as of October 2026.

solutions.title: The SeaCleaners
solutions.blurb: Mobula cleanup boats catch plastic close to where it starts, and in Malaysia one boat turned 135,000 pieces of debris into community walkways.

solutions.title: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
solutions.blurb: Tubbataha, a no-take marine park of 96,828 hectares in the Philippines, protects pristine coral atolls and the sea life that seeds the Sulu Sea (UNESCO).

solutions.title: Whales, Ocean Gardeners
solutions.blurb: Whale waste carries nutrients to the ocean surface and fertilizes phytoplankton, the tiny plants at the base of the ocean food web (NOAA Fisheries).

solutions.title: ATLAS Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System
solutions.blurb: Four robotic telescopes, two in Hawaiʻi, search the entire dark sky every 24 hours for asteroids that could hit Earth, so people can be warned.

solutions.title: Catalina Sky Survey
solutions.blurb: A NASA-funded survey in Arizona that has discovered more near-Earth objects than any other: 17,930 near-Earth asteroids since 1995.

solutions.title: Comet Interceptor (ESA / JAXA)
solutions.blurb: Three spacecraft will wait in space for a fresh comet and fly past it together to make a 3D map; launch is planned for late 2028 or early 2029 (ESA).

solutions.title: Hayabusa2 Torifune Flyby (JAXA)
solutions.blurb: On 5 July 2026, JAXA's Hayabusa2 passed about 400 m above asteroid Torifune, the closest flyby of any Solar System body so far (JAXA).

solutions.title: Hera
solutions.blurb: ESA's Hera has arrived at the Didymos asteroids to measure what NASA's DART impact did to Dimorphos, turning deflection into a repeatable defense.

solutions.title: IAU Minor Planet Center
solutions.blurb: The Minor Planet Center is the world’s clearinghouse for asteroid and comet sightings.

solutions.title: Lucy (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's Lucy is touring asteroids; after Dinkinesh and Donaldjohanson, it reaches its first Trojan asteroid, Eurybates, on 11 August 2027 (NASA).

solutions.title: Near-Earth Object Coordination Centre (ESA)
solutions.blurb: Europe's asteroid watch centre computes orbits and impact risks every day and keeps a public list of every asteroid with a non-zero chance of hitting Earth.

solutions.title: NEO Surveyor
solutions.blurb: NASA NEO Surveyor is the first space telescope built to find hazardous asteroids, including dark ones hidden in the Sun's glare.

solutions.title: NEOSSat Asteroid and Debris Telescope (Canada)
solutions.blurb: Canada's NEOSSat circles Earth every 100 minutes, scanning near the Sun for asteroids and comets and tracking satellites and debris (CSA).

solutions.title: OSIRIS-APEX and Apophis 2029 (NASA)
solutions.blurb: On April 13, 2029, asteroid Apophis passes about 20,000 miles from Earth.

solutions.title: Pan-STARRS Near-Earth Object Search
solutions.blurb: Two telescopes on Haleakalā, Maui, that in 2021 found nearly as many near-Earth objects as the rest of the world's observatories combined.

solutions.title: Ramses (ESA / JAXA)
solutions.blurb: ESA and JAXA's Ramses must launch by spring 2028 to meet Apophis before its 2029 Earth pass.

solutions.title: Vera C. Rubin Observatory
solutions.blurb: A new NSF–DOE observatory on Cerro Pachón, Chile, began its 10-year sky survey in July 2026 and is already finding asteroids by the thousand.

solutions.title: Webb and 2024 YR4
solutions.blurb: How the James Webb Space Telescope tracked asteroid 2024 YR4 in February 2026 and ruled out a 2032 Moon impact, two years before ground telescopes could.

solutions.title: Arctic Basecamp
solutions.blurb: Arctic Basecamp is a registered not-for-profit that spotlights the global threats of polar climate change and communicates areas of action.

solutions.title: Arctic Weather Satellite and EPS-Sterna (ESA/EUMETSAT)
solutions.blurb: ESA's small Arctic Weather Satellite, launched in August 2024, paved the way for EPS-Sterna, a fleet of 20 satellites from 2029 (ESA, EUMETSAT).

solutions.title: ASOC: Antarctic and Southern Ocean Coalition
solutions.blurb: ASOC, a coalition of conservation groups, has advocated for stronger protection of Antarctica and the Southern Ocean since 1978 (ASOC).

solutions.title: Beyond EPICA – Oldest Ice
solutions.blurb: The European project Beyond EPICA – Oldest Ice drills Antarctic ice to read climate and environmental history (Beyond EPICA).

solutions.title: CAFF: Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna
solutions.blurb: CAFF is the biodiversity working group of the Arctic Council (CAFF).

solutions.title: Carbfix: Turning CO2 Into Stone
solutions.blurb: Carbfix dissolves carbon dioxide in water and injects it into basalt rock, where it turns into stone (company).

solutions.title: CCAMLR: Conserving Antarctic Marine Life
solutions.blurb: CCAMLR manages Antarctic marine life with an ecosystem-based approach, allowing only sustainable harvesting that accounts for effects on the ecosystem.

solutions.title: CIMR Copernicus Imaging Microwave Radiometer (ESA)
solutions.blurb: Two Copernicus satellites will measure sea ice, sea-surface temperature and salinity over 95% of the globe every day, with sub-daily polar views (ESA).

solutions.title: CRISTAL Polar Ice and Snow Altimeter (ESA)
solutions.blurb: CRISTAL will carry the first dual-frequency radar altimeter to measure polar sea-ice thickness and the snow on top, following ESA's CryoSat (ESA).

solutions.title: CryoSat Ice Mission (ESA)
solutions.blurb: CryoSat measures polar sea ice and the great ice sheets from space, and its data revealed 85 hidden lakes under Antarctica (ESA).

solutions.title: GCOM-W "SHIZUKU" Sea-Ice Watch (JAXA)
solutions.blurb: JAXA's SHIZUKU satellite, launched in 2012, measures sea ice, rain, snow and sea temperature through clouds, day and night (JAXA).

solutions.title: Gough Island Restoration Programme
solutions.blurb: The RSPB-led Gough Island Restoration Programme tried in 2021 to remove the invasive mice that prey on seabirds.

solutions.title: IAATO: Responsible Antarctic Tourism
solutions.blurb: IAATO, founded in 1991, promotes safe and environmentally responsible private-sector travel to the Antarctic (IAATO).

solutions.title: Ice Memory Sanctuary
solutions.blurb: On 14 January 2026, the Ice Memory Sanctuary opened at Concordia Station: a 35-meter cave in the Antarctic ice, about −52 °C, with no mechanical refrigeration.

solutions.title: Iceland Land Restoration (Land and Forest Iceland)
solutions.blurb: Since 1907, Iceland's soil conservation agency, now Land and Forest Iceland, has worked with farmers to halt erosion and restore land.

solutions.title: ICESat-2 (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's ICESat-2 laser fires 10,000 pulses a second to measure ice sheets, sea ice, forests and coastal seafloor in 3D.

solutions.title: International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration
solutions.blurb: About 100 scientists from the UK, US, South Korea, Germany and Sweden are working out how fast Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier could raise sea levels (ITGC).

solutions.title: Inuit Circumpolar Council
solutions.blurb: Founded in 1977, the Inuit Circumpolar Council brings Inuit rights and priorities to the international level (ICC).

solutions.title: MOSAiC Expedition: A Year Frozen in the Arctic Ice
solutions.blurb: MOSAiC was the first year-round expedition into the central Arctic to study its climate system (MOSAiC).

solutions.title: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)
solutions.blurb: NSIDC tracks Earth’s ice.

solutions.title: Oceanites: Antarctic Penguin Census
solutions.blurb: For more than 30 years, Oceanites has tracked penguin populations on the rapidly warming Antarctic Peninsula and shares the data openly (Oceanites).

solutions.title: PAME: Protecting the Arctic Marine Environment
solutions.blurb: PAME is the Arctic Council working group for the protection and sustainable use of the Arctic marine environment (PAME).

solutions.title: Penguin Watch: Count Penguins from Home
solutions.blurb: On Penguin Watch, anyone online counts penguin adults, chicks and eggs in camera photos to help scientists understand their lives and environment.

solutions.title: Permafrost Pathways
solutions.blurb: Permafrost Pathways connects science, people and policy to address Arctic permafrost thaw and support affected communities (Permafrost Pathways).

solutions.title: Polar Bears International
solutions.blurb: Polar Bears International works through research, policy and on-the-ground conservation to protect polar bears and their sea-ice habitat.

solutions.title: PREFIRE Polar CubeSats (NASA)
solutions.blurb: Two shoebox-size NASA satellites measure the far-infrared heat that Earth's poles send into space (NASA JPL).

solutions.title: PROMICE and GC-Net: Greenland Ice-Sheet Weather Stations
solutions.blurb: PROMICE and GC-Net put automatic weather stations on the Greenland ice sheet and share the data openly (PROMICE).

solutions.title: Ross Sea Region Marine Protected Area

solutions.title: SCAR: Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research

solutions.title: Ariel Exoplanet Mission (ESA)

solutions.title: Starfish Space Otter

solutions.title: Titan

solutions.title: U.S. Deorbit Vehicle (NASA / SpaceX)
solutions.blurb: NASA selected SpaceX to build the U.S.

solutions.title: Zero Debris Charter (ESA)

solutions.title: Aditya-L1 (ISRO)

solutions.title: GOES-19 and CCOR-1 (NOAA)

solutions.title: Parker Solar Probe (NASA)

solutions.title: Proba-3

solutions.title: PUNCH (NASA)

solutions.title: SOLAR-1 (NOAA)

solutions.title: TRACERS (NASA)

solutions.title: Vigil (ESA)
